v1_changes.change: Weekly 3/5/7 % chosen each week by the person's state (fatigue, life, response), never by muscle size; coach/client can set 0-7 % by hand (10 % is never offered as a rate: 'way too much', UNI-05; v1 verification); every size-class rate retired
The % is of weekly sets per muscle; load and volume load tracked, not driven by %
10 %/week is a hard ceiling on total weekly resistance sets (was INFERRED smoothing); a week must stay BELOW +10 % (a +10 % week is what he called 'way too much'; v1 verification)
Bank the fraction, release a whole set at 1.0 (v0 released at 0.75)

New set goes to the first exercise in session order, then the next (2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3); 3-4 exercises per muscle group on its day; small muscle at the end of a session -> bonus exercise

One 10/10 set = 1 set to the primary muscle (RFE lunge -> quads; glute credit undecided); alternating = unilateral
Athletic patterns never count toward muscle sets; the v0 0.5 fatigue-budget charge is retired
Leg curls / nordics / slider curls = leg-flexion segment, not hip dominant
Weekly sets per muscle are STARTING volumes: beginner 10-12, intermediate 15-20, advanced 20+; 15-20 = maintenance to some growth, 20-25 = growth; v0 peak-week table and L4 retired
Priority +4-6 sets on the start, cap ~25-30, 1-2 at a time, first in session; delivery own exercises -> Focus slots -> bonus; v0 +2 rate points retired
Pain: -30 to -50 %, constrained machines or split grips, drop the exercise if still too much; swapped lift keeps sets ideally, adjust accordingly
Calves 3 sets every leg day; rear delts own sets; ~2 core exercises per session, first by default
Chest-low / side-delt-high template pattern not intended: balance to the start table; V-taper bias optional (mechanism PROPOSED)

Session caps by population: resistance 5-7 exercises; field athletes off-season up to 10-12 (2 core + 2-4 plyo/ballistic + 2-3 Olympic/power + 3-4 resistance); ~90 min (max 120) athletes/bodybuilders/powerlifters; 45-60 min general/weight loss; unilateral time accounted for; v0 minutes-by-level table retired
Default sets: 3 compound, 2 isolation, 3 calves, 2 per slot in athletic templates
Reps: small 12-30, big 5-15 mixed; 40-rep sets removed from defaults, optional CrossFit/AMRAP style only
Preference moves big-compound reps only; weekly sets unchanged (v0 x1.1 / x0.85 removed); small muscles stay high-rep
Unilateral moderate-high reps by default; heavy low-rep unilateral optional toggle; unilateral progresses like bilateral
RIR primary, 1-3 RIR on every working set, no planned ramp; MAX = technical failure only on small-muscle or bodyweight work; RPE explained alongside; % in strength/Olympic templates
Rest: hypertrophy 1-2 min (up to 3), strength 3-6 min, athletic as prescribed, supersets after the pair
MYO only on the last exercise, machine or isolation
Aerobic sessions/week: 3 general/fat loss, 2 athletes in season, 4 aesthetics/bodybuilders + long walks after workouts; any erg, calories/time/distance
Deload = about half the sets, lighter or 3+ RIR, no buy-out/finisher (v0 0.85 x week 1 retired; observed shapes kept as evidence)
Plan lengths: 4-6 wk maintenance/transition 50-70 %; 8 wk start hard 4+4; 12 wk preferred 2-4 / 4-6 / hardest last; week-by-week; yearly; v0 6/8/12 layouts retired
Smooth weekly adds for hypertrophy/general; 2-week steps/waves for fight or competition prep
Levels L1-L3 (novice = newby; 6-12+ months off -> L1 body; ex-pros L1 briefly); L4 and 'NOVICE below NEWBY' retired
Plyo labels are not zones; method stages receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated (RC1-RC3, name PROPOSED); unilateral harder; start ballistic, end plyometric
Sport dial by ground-contact time and ATH-02 ranking (baseball now below MMA/tennis); Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training; boxers reduce, never cut, pressing/arms
No medball for aesthetics/bodybuilders except warm-up; medballs <= 20 lb
No bands / variable resistance in any generator rule; banded items kept as evidence only
Older clients: few plyos unless requested; constrained machines; no overhead squat/snatch/low-bar/depth jumps; no sex-based rules
Rep notation: 10/10 = per side; '12/10/8 -20' = pyramid + light 20; same rep rules at every level (UL upper rise = fill error)
VOL 1/2/3 rep phases for all athletes, one per block
Adjust from EFFORT / HOW IT FELT confirmed; person-level rate; two output modes PROPOSED (GEN-03 vs GEN-05)
'21.6 mile run' = marathon per coach (flag: marathon = 26.2 mi)
A 'MYO SET' counts as 2 hard sets (stated so 03 matches 12 counting; INFERRED), only on the last machine or isolation exercise
Same-pattern pairing (squat + lunge) allowed for aesthetics/high-level clients to drive one muscle harder; cross-pattern for bootcamp/general

No second axial squat in a week for every population (squat once; leg press/belt squat the other day); deadlifts also load the spine, so one axial hinge a week, other hinge exposure non-axial (05 rule 18; reading INFERRED); hip dominant + push / knee dominant + pull on every full-body and bootcamp day (v1 had both only for general clients)

counting.science_support: Pelland et al. (SportRxiv 460 v2 2024; journal version Sports Med): fractional (0.5) counting of indirect sets had the strongest relative evidence. Ramirez-Campillo et al. 2023 (Sports, 12 studies): plyometric training did not change muscle mass in combat-sport athletes (ES -0.01 to -0.06). Counter-evidence: Grgic, Schoenfeld, Mikulic 2021 (J Sport Health Sci) found plyometric and resistance training produced similar lower-body hypertrophy in untrained/recreational samples (up to 12 weeks). Coach count differs: helpers 0.25 (COACH-ANSWER VOL-09) vs Pelland 0.5; the engine steers on the coach count and stores the 0.5 count beside it (12 > counting.dual_count, PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL).

science_reference.rp_mesocycle: start near MEV; add sets when recovery is early and performance stable; advanced RP coaches add only ~2-3 sets per muscle per session over a 4-week accumulation; 3 sets/muscle/session gives MEV-level gains for most beginner-intermediates
volume_dose_response: Schoenfeld et al. 2019 MSSE: 1/3/5 sets per exercise 3x/wk (6-9 / 18-27 / 30-45 weekly sets): hypertrophy rises with volume, strength similar
Baz-Valle et al. 2022: 12-20 weekly sets recommended; >20 no extra benefit for quads/biceps (triceps exception)

Pelland et al. (SportRxiv 460, 67 studies; journal version Sports Med): positive dose-response with diminishing returns (stronger for strength); fractional counting had the strongest relative evidence; frequency matters for strength, negligible for hypertrophy
Remmert et al. 2025 preprint: per-session PUOS ~11 fractional sets (hypertrophy), ~2 direct sets (strength)
Ralston et al. 2017: >=6 sets/exercise/week slightly better for strength than <=5
science_reference.frequency: Schoenfeld et al. 2019: frequency has little effect on hypertrophy when volume is equated; practical minimum 2x/week per muscle. Coach: 2x/week in 4-6 day templates, but 1x/week for several patterns in the 3-day builder and 3-day PPL variants (OBSERVED)
science_reference.loading: Schoenfeld, Grgic, Van Every, Plotkin 2021: similar hypertrophy from ~5 to 30+ reps if sets equated and close to failure; strength favours heavy loads
effort: Zourdos et al. 2016: RPE 10 = 0 RIR, 9 = 1 RIR, 8 = 2 RIR
Robinson et al. (2023 preprint): hypertrophy improves closer to failure; strength insensitive
Refalo et al. 2024: failure vs 1-2 RIR similar growth; failure more fatigue
rest: Singer et al. 2024: small benefit >60 s, no further benefit >90 s for hypertrophy
NSCA plyo: work:rest 1:5-1:10; depth jumps 5-10 s between reps, 2-3 min between sets; 48-72 h between plyo sessions
deload: Rogerson, Bell et al. 2024: deload every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks, 6.4 +/- 1.7 days, volume cut via reps and sets, frequency kept, mostly pre-planned
Bell et al. 2023 Delphi: deload = period of reduced training stress to mitigate fatigue and enhance preparedness
science_reference.maintenance: Spiering et al. 2021: strength and size maintained up to 32 weeks with 1 session/week and 1 set/exercise if intensity is kept (younger adults) (younger adults; older adults needed ~2 sessions/week and 2-3 sets to keep muscle size)
plyometrics: NSCA (CSCS ch. 18 summary, PT Pioneer; same numbers on a SUNY Cortland page without citation): 80-100 (beginner), 100-120 (intermediate), 120-140 (advanced) contacts per session; off-season 2-3 sessions/wk (football), 3-4 (track); in-season 1 / 2-3
de Villarreal et al. 2009: >10 weeks, >20 sessions, >50 jumps per session maximised vertical-jump gains
youth basketball: 49 vs 99 jumps/session similar gains
Ramirez-Campillo et al. 2023 (Sports, 12 studies; combat sports): 2-3 sessions/wk, 4-12 wks; jump, strength, COD up; muscle mass unchanged (ES -0.01 to -0.06)

Grgic, Schoenfeld, Mikulic 2021 (J Sport Health Sci 10(5)): plyometric and resistance training produced similar lower-body hypertrophy in untrained/recreational samples (6 comparison studies, up to 12 weeks)
conditioning: Seiler: elite endurance athletes ~80 % low / 20 % high intensity
Wilson et al. 2012: interference with strength/power/hypertrophy grows with endurance frequency and duration
science_reference.pat_davidson: His link in the coach's answers is the zones of 'A Coach's Guide to Optimizing Movement': rotation biases of body positions (vertical/arms overhead/deep squat = external-rotation bias; horizontal/hands in front/half squat = zone 2, internal-rotation bias, compressive) used for exercise level by load position; they do not apply to plyos and levels are still theoretical (COACH-ANSWER CAT-04, CAT-05, CAT-10). Shapes exercise level, not dose; no Davidson dosing number used.
